title: Report: Reshape Automation finds that leading AI models score at most 52% on industrial parts questions
source_used: Robotics 24/7 (page tagged Press Release; text read from the fulltext copy)
key_facts: Reshape Automation, builder of the ReshapeX sales-acceleration platform for automation OEMs, system integrators and distributors, released the Industrial AI Accuracy Index 2026.
It tested three AI models (GPT-6 Astra, Claude and Gemini) on 100 questions drawn from what customers ask distributors and OEMs, covering parts from 14 industrial manufacturers.
From memory alone the models got 12% to 14% right; with web search the best scored 52%, and about 1 in 3 wrong answers gave a specific part number or figure with no caveat.
Reshape's engineers wrote the questions and no third party reviewed them; the answer key comes from ReshapeX's own answers, verified against manufacturer documentation.
Reshape says its ReshapeX platform is not scored on equal terms with the models it tested.

Each model ran through its provider's API with a pinned model ID in 1,500 calls on 24 Sep 2026; Gemini ran without web search because its provider's terms require written permission to benchmark with grounding.

A model drafted each grade and Reshape's engineers made the final call; the report lists 13 limitations and prints all 100 questions plus a SHA-256 fingerprint of the answer key, which is withheld but available on request.

CEO Juan Aparicio said parts answers depend on relationships between facts held in different places, so a model rebuilding them each time is sometimes right and sometimes wrong while sounding equally sure.
quote_evidence: From memory alone, the models got 12% to 14% right.
The company said that its ReshapeX platform is not scored on equal terms with the models it tested.
why_it_matters_hint: One vendor's own test suggests general chatbots often give confident but wrong industrial part answers, which matters to distributors who must check every answer.
event_date: Tests run on 24 Sep 2026; the article (dated 11 Oct 2026) does not give the release date.
notes: The page is a company press release (tagged Press Release on Robotics 24/7); the report itself was not opened. The company that ran the test sells a product it says is not scored on equal terms.
